test.title: Motion in One Dimension - Test 2
test.description: Previous Year Questions as Chapter Test
test.syllabus: This test contains questions from all topics of this chapter included in the JEE Main syllabus. It includes a mix of questions from PYQs of JEE Main 2019 - 2025.

question.text: A balloon is moving up in air vertically above a point A on the ground. When it is a height h1, a girl standing at a distance d (point B) from A (see figure) sees it at an angle 45° with respect to the vertical. When the balloon climbs up a further height h2, it is seen at an angle 60° with respect to the vertical if the girl moves further by a distance 2.464 d (point C). Then the height h2 is (given tan30°=0.5774):

A ball is thrown vertically upward with an initial velocity of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>150</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The ratio of velocity after <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>x</mi></mfrac></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is _____. {take, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>}

A NCC parade is going at a uniform speed of 9 km h-1 under a mango tree on which a monkey is sitting at a height of 19.6 m. At any particular instant, the monkey drops a mango. A cadet will receive the mango whose distance from the tree at time of drop is :
(Given g=9.8 m s-2)

A car accelerates from rest at a constant rate <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>α</mi></math> for some time after which it decelerates at a constant rate <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>β</mi></math> to come to rest. If the total time elapsed is t seconds, the total distance travelled is:

The position of a particle as a function of time <math><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo></math> is given by <math><mi>x</mi><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfenced><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><msup><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>-</mo><mi>c</mi><msup><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></math> where <math><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi> </mi><mi>b</mi></math> and <math><mi>c</mi></math> are constants. When the particles zero acceleration, then its velocity will be:

Train A is moving along two parallel rail tracks towards north with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>72</mn><mo> </mo><mi>km</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">h</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> and train <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> is moving towards south with speed <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>108</mn><mo> </mo><mi>km</mi><mo> </mo><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">h</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. Velocity of train <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> with respect to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> and velocity of ground with respect to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> are (in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>):

The displacement x versus time graph is shown below.

(A) The average velocity during 0 to 3 s is $10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$
(B) The average velocity during 3 to 5 s is $0 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$
(C) The instantaneous velocity at $\mathrm{t}=2 \mathrm{~s}$ is $5 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$
(D) The average velocity during 5 to 7 s and instantaneous velocity at $\mathrm{t}=6.5 \mathrm{~s}$ are equal
(E) The average velocity from $t=0$ to $t=9 \mathrm{~s}$ is zero
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

A train starting from rest first accelerates uniformly up to a speed of $80 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{h}$ for time $t$, then it moves with a constant speed for time $3 t$. The average speed of the train for this duration of journey will be (in $\mathrm{km} / \mathrm{h}$ ) :

The distance travelled by a particle is related to time <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi></math> as <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo> </mo><mo>=</mo><mo> </mo><mn>4</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>. The velocity of the particle at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi><mo> </mo><mo>=</mo><mo> </mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math> is

An elevator in a building can carry a maximum of <math><mn>10</mn></math> persons, with the average mass of each person being <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>68</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">k</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> . The mass of the elevator itself is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>920</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">k</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> and it moves with a constant speed of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo>/</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math> . The frictional force opposing the motion is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>6000</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></math> . If the elevator is moving up with its full capacity, the power delivered by the motor to the elevator <math><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow><mo>/</mo><mrow><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow></mfenced></math> must be at least:

A particle of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>M</mi></math> originally at rest is subjected to a force whose direction is constant but magnitude varies with time according to the relation <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>F</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mfenced open="[" close="]"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>-</mo><msup><mfenced><mfrac><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow><mi>T</mi></mfrac></mfenced><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfenced></math> where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>T</mi></math> are constants. The force acts only for the time interval <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi>T</mi></math>. The velocity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>v</mi></math> of the particle after time <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi>T</mi></math> is:

A passenger sitting in a train A moving at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>90</mn><mo> </mo><mi>km</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">h</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> observes another train B moving in the opposite direction for <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>8</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math>. If the velocity of the train B is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>54</mn><mo> </mo><mi>km</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">h</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>, then length of train B is:

The position vector of a particle changes with time according to the relation <math><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo>→</mo></mover><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfenced><mo>=</mo><mn>15</mn><msup><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>i</mi></mrow><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>+</mo><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>20</mn><msup><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mfenced><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>j</mi></mrow><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>.</mo></math> What is the magnitude of the acceleration at <math><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>?</mo></math>

The velocity-displacement graph describing the motion of a bicycle is shown in the figure.

The acceleration-displacement graph of the bicycle's motion is best described by :

A juggler throws balls vertically upwards with same initial velocity in air. When the first ball reaches its highest position, he throws the next ball. Assuming the juggler throws <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>n</mi></math> balls per second, the maximum height the balls can reach is

A particle moves along the $x$-axis and has its displacement $x$ varying with time $t$ according to the equation $\mathrm{x}=\mathrm{c}_0\left(\mathrm{t}^2-2\right)+\mathrm{c}(\mathrm{t}-2)^2$ where $c_0$ and $c$ are constants of appropriate dimensions. Then, which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: the acceleration of the particle is $2 \mathrm{c}_0$
the acceleration of the particle is $2\mathrm{~c}$
the initial velocity of the particle is $4\mathrm{~c}$
the acceleration of the particle is $2\left(c+c_0\right)$

question.text: The relation between time ‘<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi></math>’ and distance ‘<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math>’ is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>α</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>β</mi><mi>x</mi></math>, where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>α</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>β</mi></math> are constants. The relation between acceleration <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mi>a</mi></mfenced></math> and velocity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mi>v</mi></mfenced></math> is:

A person travels <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> distance with velocity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>v</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> and then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> distance with velocity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>v</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> in the same direction. The average velocity of the person is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>v</mi></math>, then the relation between <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>v</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>v</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> will be

question.text: The velocity (v) and time (t) graph of a body in a straight line motion is shown in the figure. The point S is at 4.333 seconds. The total distance covered by the body in 6 s is :
An object is thrown vertically upwards. At its maximum height, which of the following quantity becomes zero ?

A boy pushes a box of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> with a force <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mover><mi>F</mi><mo>→</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mfenced><mrow><mn>20</mn><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>+</mo><mn>10</mn><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">j</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></mrow></mfenced><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></math> on a frictionless surface. If the box was initially at rest, then _______ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> is displacement along the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math>-axis after <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math>

From the top of a tower, a ball is thrown vertically upward which reaches the ground in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>6</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math>. A second ball thrown vertically downward from the same position with the same speed reaches the ground in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math>. A third ball released, from the rest from the same location, will reach the ground in _____ s.

The distance <math><mi>x</mi></math> covered by a paritcle in one dimensional motion varies with time <math><mi>t</mi></math> as <math><msup><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><msup><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>b</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi></math> . If the acceleration of the particle depends on <math><mi>x</mi></math> as <math><msup><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></msup></math> , where <math><mi>n</mi></math> is an integer, the value of <math><mi>n</mi></math> is _________

A person travelling on a straight line moves with a uniform velocity $\mathrm{v}_1$ for a distance x and with a uniform velocity $\mathrm{v}_2$ for the next $\frac{3}{2} \mathrm{x}$ distance. The average velocity in this motion is $\frac{50}{7} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$. If $\mathrm{v}_1$ is $5 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ then $\mathrm{v}_2=$ _________ $\mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}$.
A particle is moving with constant acceleration a. Following graph shows v2 versus x (displacement) plot. The acceleration of the particle is _________ m s-2.
